title: Understanding N-grams
text: Think about how N-grams work. They capture sequences of letters, but do they consider the biological significance of codons?

title: Codons and Amino Acids
text: Remember that codons are groups of $$3$$ letters. How might this affect the usefulness of capturing sequences of $$1$$ or $$2$$ letters?

title: Overlapping Segments
text: Consider the sequence ATGCA. How would a 3-gram encoding break this sequence into words?

hintAnswer: It could suggest unrelated sequences like AGA.
title: Non-Consecutive Segments
text: If N-grams capture non-consecutive segments, what might be a potential issue with the sequence ATGCA?
choices: It could suggest unrelated sequences like AGA.
It captures all possible codons accurately.

hintAnswer: $$N-gram$$ might capture $$wrap-around$$ segments like TGG from GGTT.
title: Wrap-Around Segments
text: Does DNA wrap around like a circle, or is it linear? How might this affect N-gram encoding?
choices: $$N-gram$$ might capture $$wrap-around$$ segments like TGG from GGTT.
DNA naturally wraps around, so $$N-gram$$ is accurate.
